clue.text: Drives rig dressed in a green coat

indicators.note: to dress something is to arrange or prepare it, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A driver gives a lorry rig a fresh coat of green paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' rearranges DRIVES RIG into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluish-green film that forms on weathered copper or brass is a coating of patina.

clue.text: Reserve put on some teddy bears?

explanation.surface: A note about keeping something aside, and about soft toys.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside for a purpose; also, literally, a tag fixed in a toy bear's ear, as on a famous maker's teddies.

clue.text: Notice that English sailors are under record

indicators.note: in a down clue pieces under another come after it

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
RN, the Royal Navy, is the body of British sailors

explanation.surface: A remark that English sailors are lower down a list.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'are under' places E and RN below DISC.
explanation.definitionFit: To perceive or make out something, a verb in both cases.

clue.text: Speaks in support of benefit disputes

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits beneath, so it comes after

parts.note: a gain is a benefit
says means speaks

explanation.surface: Someone argues for an advantage and then contradicts it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'in support of' puts SAYS beneath GAIN. 'Speaks in support of' looks like 'argues for', which is the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or contradict, so both are verbs of contesting a claim.

clue.text: Break away from predecessors in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the run is read from right to left
the letters are taken out of the middle of the following word

explanation.surface: Breaking with the people who came before in a backward movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' picks EDECES out of predecessors; 'in retreat' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw formally from a federation or union, as states did before the American Civil War.

clue.text: The red baron was one pretentious person on my list!

parts.note: a pseud is a pretentious person, a British slang term
taken as written

indicators.note: a ship that lists leans over, here tipping the word so it reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A snob boasts that the First World War flying ace is on his roster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' tips the possessive word over so it reads backwards. 'The red baron' was the nickname of the German pilot Manfred von Richthofen, not his real name, which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A false or adopted name, like the nickname given to the German fighter pilot.

clue.text: Only some are showing favouritism!

explanation.surface: A remark that only a few people are biased.
explanation.definitionFit: Incomplete rather than whole; also biased in favour of one side.

clue.text: Do they hunt with the home counties bowmen?

parts.note: the home counties surround London in the south-east of England, SE
archers are bowmen

explanation.surface: A question whether archers from around London go hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are the counties surrounding London, in the south-east (SE) of England.
explanation.definitionFit: People who look for something, hunting it out.

clue.text: Capture east European found in Newcastle

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it, so the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: NE is the postcode area of Newcastle upon Tyne
a Slav is a native of eastern Europe

explanation.surface: Police arrest an eastern European tracked down in Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' signals the container; Newcastle upon Tyne is a city in north-east England whose postcode area supplies the outer letters, and east goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To take people captive and hold them in bondage is to make slaves of them.

clue.text: Paid sportsmen backing agents — that's commonplace!

parts.note: professionals, or pros, are sportsmen who are paid

indicators.note: going backwards, so the agents' letters are read from the end

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, a body of agents

explanation.surface: Professional athletes supporting their agents is nothing out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the American intelligence agency to give AIC; 'Paid sportsmen' suggests the definition, but it is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and ordinary, lacking any imagination, like plain prose rather than poetry.

clue.text: Line that's almost the same height?

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: equal means the same
a tor is a rocky hill or height, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A question about a line drawn at nearly the same level throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter; a tor is a craggy hilltop on the moors of south-west England. The question mark flags that the line is imaginary.
explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary circle round the Earth halfway between the poles is a line of latitude.

clue.text: Cast on Adam's ale reach critical point

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: Adam's ale is a jocular old name for water, the only drink of the first man
to cast skin or leaves is to shed them

explanation.surface: Instructions about casting a spell on water to bring it to boiling point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adam's ale' is a traditional nickname for water; 'on' puts SHED after it, and 'reach' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A turning point where events change course, from the ridge that divides two river basins.

clue.text: Illegal drug transport

explanation.surface: A banned pill taken to a high.
explanation.definitionFit: The club drug MDMA, and a state of rapture, as in being carried away with joy.

clue.text: Memorial path once beaten

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A memorial stands by a path that was once well trodden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' rearranges PATH ONCE; a beaten path is a natural phrase, which hides the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument honouring war dead whose remains lie elsewhere, like the one in Whitehall.

clue.text: Thin fleece, navy on the outside

parts.note: a fleece is the skin of a sheep

indicators.note: only the outside of the word is wanted, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A thin fleece jacket in navy blue, worn on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the outside' takes the first and last letters of navy, N and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Very lean, with little flesh on the bones.

clue.text: Launch full of drugs?

explanation.surface: Setting off a vessel loaded with narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch is a motor vessel; jokingly, a boat full of speed, the amphetamine.

clue.text: Of course, friend appears after a turn-around!

indicators.note: the friend comes after the other piece in the answer
turned around, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend shows up, of course, after a reversal of fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges A TURN into NATUR; 'turn-around' reads as one word in the surface, which hides the split between fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Used to say something is as expected, without question.

clue.text: A high tar's place and a shy tar's place?

indicators.note: to place things is to arrange them, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: a timid sailor, the possessive adding no letters

explanation.surface: Two riddles: where a strong cigarette goes, and where a timid sailor belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: A high-tar cigarette ends up in this dish; 'tar' then switches to its sailor sense, and the shy sailor's letters rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The receptacle where a smoker taps ash and stubs out a high-tar cigarette.

clue.text: The fool suffered, and was attacked

parts.note: an ass is a fool
ailed means suffered or was unwell

explanation.surface: An idiot was in pain and had been set upon.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a past participle, matching 'was attacked'.
explanation.definitionFit: Set upon violently, physically or with criticism.

clue.text: Understand about steamship and wander off

parts.note: dig is slang for understand
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A passenger grasps something about a ship and goes off on a tangent.
explanation.walkthrough: DIG for 'understand' is 1960s slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray from the main subject in talk or writing.

clue.text: Fumes, on seeing donkey on board ship!

indicators.note: a passenger on board is inside the vessel, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
moke is a British slang word for a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone is furious to find a donkey travelling aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The donkey is British slang, a moke; 'on board' puts it inside the steamship abbreviation. 'Fumes' looks like anger but means gives off smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: To fume is to give off smoke or vapour, the verb sense in both words.

clue.text: Sentiment no one backs after work at home

indicators.note: the reversed pieces follow the others in the answer

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
in means at home

indicators.note: to back is to move backwards, so the words no and one are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A feeling that nobody supports working from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' reads NO plus I backwards to give ION, which 'after' places at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A view or feeling held about something.

clue.text: Teams getting the Spanish odds!

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
evens are betting odds of one to one

explanation.surface: Football squads get the Spanish betting prices.
explanation.walkthrough: Evens is a betting price where the stake is doubled on a win, a paradox with 'odds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket and football sides each have this many players, so they are named by it.

clue.text: Gourmets big film sure to be developed

parts.note: an epic is a big, sweeping film

indicators.note: film that is developed is processed and changed, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Food critics are sure that the big film will be developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be developed' rearranges SURE into URES; the photographic sense of 'developed' keeps the film picture consistent and disguises the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: People devoted to refined food and drink, named after the pleasure-seeking philosopher Epicurus.

clue.text: Goes round and round, being terribly one-sided — not on!

indicators.note: terribly signals that the letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: the word on is removed from the letters

explanation.surface: A complaint that a spinning contest is badly lopsided and unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges ONE-SIDED, and 'not on' removes O and N from the pool, leaving the answer's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that eddies swirls in small circular currents.

clue.text: Sets charge for noisy eater with small children

indicators.note: noisy means heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: a diner is someone eating a meal
mites are small children

explanation.surface: A restaurant bills a loud customer extra for bringing along youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noisy' asks for the spoken sound of a restaurant customer, entered as DYNA. 'charge' reads as a bill but is an explosive charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow something up with explosive is to lay a charge against it.

clue.text: One who serves the legal profession (young girl)

parts.note: barristers as a body are called the Bar
a maid is an old word for a young girl

explanation.surface: Someone working in service to lawyers, a young girl herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the legal profession' is the collective name for barristers in Britain; the bracketed girl looks like an aside but completes the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who pours drinks behind the counter of a pub.

clue.text: Less attractive, but more obvious

explanation.surface: A comment on something both uglier and easier to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain can mean homely in looks or clear and evident; this is the comparative of both senses.

clue.text: Answer given to sailor let off the hook

indicators.note: the answer is given to the sailor, so it is attached after him

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
to answer a puzzle is to solve it

explanation.surface: A sailor, given an answer, is cleared of blame.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is the usual crossword sailor; SOLVE is the verb sense of 'Answer'.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone from guilt or punishment, as a priest forgives sins.

clue.text: Look to eat sandwiches outside, in squalor

parts.note: to look is to see
to dine is to eat

indicators.note: only the outside of the word is wanted, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Advice to eat sandwiches outdoors in grim surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' takes the first and last letters of sandwiches, S and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabbiness and dirt, the state of a run-down, disreputable place.
